modules.name: ShortenService
modules.responsibility: Create short codes for long URLs, enforce uniqueness, validate and normalize input URLs, and resolve a short code back to its target URL.

modules.name: CodeGenerator
modules.responsibility: Produce collision-resistant, URL-safe short codes from an internal id or random source. Pluggable strategy (base62 counter, random, hashids).

modules.name: RedirectHandler
modules.responsibility: Handle inbound GET /{code} requests: look up the target, emit a click event, and issue a 301/302 redirect or 404 for unknown codes.
interfaces:
class RedirectHandler(Protocol):
    def handle(self, code: str, ctx: RequestContext) -> RedirectResult: ...

modules.name: StatsService
modules.responsibility: Record click events and aggregate per-link statistics (total clicks, last-clicked, breakdown by day). Decoupled from the redirect hot path.

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Enforce per-client request quotas on write (shorten) and redirect endpoints using a token-bucket / fixed-window strategy keyed by client identity.
interfaces:
class RateLimiter(Protocol):
    def allow(self, key: str, *, cost: int = 1) -> RateDecision: ...

modules.name: APIGateway
modules.responsibility: HTTP boundary: route requests, parse/validate payloads, apply RateLimiter, map domain results and errors to HTTP responses (JSON for API, redirect for /{code}).

fields.name: id
fields.note: internal monotonic id, source for base62 code

data_model.name: ClickEvent

fields.name: ip_hash
fields.note: salted hash of client IP, never raw IP

relationships: many ClickEvent belong to one ShortLink

data_model.name: LinkStats
relationships: derived aggregate over ClickEvent for a code

fields.name: key
fields.note: client identity (hashed IP or API key)

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL (API)
steps: Gateway applies rate limit for client key
ShortenService validates and normalizes the URL
CodeGenerator produces a unique code; link persisted
ux_flows.success_criteria: Valid URL returns a working short_url in a single request with HTTP 201
i18n_considerations: Error messages returned via i18n message keys

ux_flows.name: Follow a short link (redirect)
steps: Respond 302 Location: long_url, or 404 if unknown/expired
ux_flows.success_criteria: Known code redirects to destination in <50ms p95 without blocking on stats write

ux_flows.name: View click stats (API)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Returns total clicks and per-day breakdown for an existing code

customer_journey: A developer integrating link-shortening posts a long URL to /api/shorten and immediately receives a compact short_url. They share it; recipients click and are redirected near-instantly to the original destination while a click is logged out of band. Later the developer queries /api/stats/{code} to see how many people clicked and the daily trend. Throughout, rate limiting protects the service from abuse without impacting honest single requests, and no raw personal data (IPs) is stored — only salted hashes for aggregate counts.

experience_metric.name: time-to-short-url
experience_metric.target: Shorten a URL in 1 API request; redirect p95 latency < 50ms; stats retrievable in 1 request

architecture_decisions.title: Decouple click-stats recording from the redirect hot path
architecture_decisions.context: The redirect endpoint is latency-sensitive and high-volume, yet every redirect must produce a click event for stats. Recording synchronously to a datastore on each redirect couples request latency to write throughput and risks failures on the critical path.
architecture_decisions.decision: RedirectHandler emits click events to a StatsRecorder behind a Protocol, implemented as fire-and-forget (in-process queue/buffer with batched flush). The redirect responds as soon as the URL is resolved, independent of stats persistence.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Keeps redirect latency low and resilient: a stats backend hiccup degrades analytics, not the core redirect function. The Protocol boundary lets us swap in-memory buffering for a real queue (e.g. Redis/Kafka) without touching redirect logic.
consequences: Click counts are eventually consistent (small lag, possible loss on crash before flush)
Need a flush/buffer component with backpressure handling
Stats and redirect can scale and fail independently
Testing redirect no longer requires a real stats store

architecture_decisions.title: Generate short codes via base62 over an internal monotonic id
architecture_decisions.context: Codes must be unique, short, URL-safe, and cheap to generate. Options: random codes (collision checks), hashing (collision risk), or encoding a sequential id.
architecture_decisions.decision: Use base62 encoding of an internal monotonic integer id as the default CodeGenerator strategy, behind a Protocol so random/custom-alias strategies remain pluggable.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Guarantees uniqueness without collision retries, produces compact codes, and is deterministic and trivially testable. The Protocol preserves flexibility for unguessable random codes where enumeration is a concern.
consequences: Sequential codes are enumerable (mitigated by optional random strategy / obfuscation)
Requires a reliable monotonic id source (DB sequence)
Very short codes for early links

threat_model.description: Open-redirect / malicious destination: attacker shortens links to phishing or malware sites, abusing the service's domain reputation.
threat_model.mitigation: Validate and normalize URLs, enforce http(s) scheme, optional domain denylist/safe-browsing check, and a max-length cap. Surface destination on a preview path.

threat_model.description: Flooding /api/shorten or /{code} to exhaust storage or capacity (mass link creation, redirect spam).
threat_model.mitigation: Per-client token-bucket rate limiting on write and redirect endpoints, with stricter quotas on shorten; return 429 with Retry-After.

threat_model.description: Click logs containing raw client IPs and user agents could expose visitor identity/behavior if leaked.
threat_model.mitigation: Never store raw IP — only a salted hash; truncate user agents; classify ClickEvent as PII with retention limits and an erasure path.

privacy_inventory.purpose: Abuse detection and de-duplicated click counting
privacy_inventory.retention: Stored only as salted hash; raw IP never persisted
privacy_inventory.encryption: Salted SHA-256 hash; salt stored separately and encrypted at rest
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Delete ClickEvents by code or by ip_hash on request; hash rotation invalidates linkage

privacy_inventory.retention: 90 days, then aggregated and rows purged
privacy_inventory.encryption: At rest via storage-level encryption; truncated to remove fine-grained entropy
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Purged by retention job or on per-code deletion
Deleting the ShortLink removes it and cascades to its ClickEvents

i18n_plan.framework: gettext-style message catalogs keyed by message id
i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: RTL supported for landing/error pages (e.g. ar) via dir=auto; API payloads are locale-neutral (ISO-8601 dates, machine codes)
i18n_plan.notes: IDN/punycode handled at URL normalization; error responses carry i18n keys, not hardcoded strings

open_questions: Should short codes be enumerable (base62 over id) or unguessable (random) by default — does the threat model require non-enumerability?
Are custom aliases a required feature in iteration 0 or deferred?
Do links expire by default, and what is the default TTL (if any)?
What is the client identity for rate limiting — IP, API key, or both — and is authentication in scope?
Is durable/at-least-once click recording required, or is best-effort (possible loss on crash) acceptable for stats?
What storage backend is targeted (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) for iteration 0?

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: url-shortener: shorten URLs, redirect via short code, record and report click stats, with rate limiting to prevent abuse. Six modules: ShortenService, CodeGenerator, RedirectHandler, StatsService, RateLimiter, APIGateway, all wired via Protocol interfaces for dependency injection.

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: ShortenService (create/resolve) -> LinkRepository, CodeGenerator. RedirectHandler (GET /{code}) -> ShortenService + StatsRecorder (async). StatsService (record/read clicks) -> ClickRepository. RateLimiter (token-bucket per client). APIGateway (HTTP boundary, validation, routing, rate limiting). CodeGenerator is a pluggable Protocol (base62 default).

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: ShortLink(id, code unique, long_url, created_at, creator_key?, expires_at?). ClickEvent(id, code FK, timestamp, ip_hash?, user_agent?, referrer?) — PII. LinkStats aggregate(total_clicks, last_clicked_at, clicks_by_day). RateBucket(key, tokens, window_start).

sections.title: Key Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 decouples stats recording from the redirect hot path (fire-and-forget behind a Protocol) for low latency and independent failure. ADR-002 uses base62 over a monotonic id for collision-free short codes, with the strategy pluggable for unguessable random codes.

sections.title: Privacy & Security
sections.content: Top threats: open-redirect (URL validation + scheme/denylist), DoS (per-client rate limiting, 429), info disclosure of click logs (salted IP hash, UA truncation, retention + erasure). PII = client IP (hashed only) and user agent (90-day retention). Deletion of a ShortLink cascades to ClickEvents.

sections.title: Digest
sections.content: url-shortener (iter 0). Modules: ShortenService, CodeGenerator (base62/pluggable), RedirectHandler, StatsService (async, decoupled), RateLimiter (token-bucket), APIGateway. Data: ShortLink(code unique, long_url), ClickEvent(PII: ip_hash, UA), LinkStats aggregate, RateBucket. Flows: POST /api/shorten -> 201 short_url; GET /{code} -> 302 + async click log; GET /api/stats/{code}. Metric: shorten in 1 request, redirect p95 <50ms. ADR-001 decouple stats from redirect hot path; ADR-002 base62 codes over monotonic id. Threats: open-redirect (URL validation), DoS (rate limit/429), click-log disclosure (salted IP hash, UA truncation, 90d retention, erasure via link delete). Open Qs: enumerable vs random codes, custom aliases, default TTL, rate-limit identity, durable vs best-effort click recording, storage backend.
